company.guidanceNotes: No formal EBITDA guidance. Known by 30-Sep-2026: both projects in Q2FY27; ~80% utilisation by Q4FY27; FY27 capex Rs800-1,000 cr; deleveraging from FY27; Equinor savings ~Rs300 cr a year at full transition.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment model on the company's reported Ind AS segments: (1) Chemicals (TAN for mining explosives, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia, Australian blasting services; held in DFPCL standalone and Deepak Mining Solutions) and (2) Fertilisers (Mahadhan AgriTech: NP/NPK, specialty and traded fertilisers), plus Realty & others. Segment EBITDA = reported segment EBIT + segment D&A (FY26 annual report note 48); 'unallocated' = sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA (corporate costs and the other income that sits inside segment results). The Chemicals revenue path is built bottom-up from TAN volume x realisation, industrial chemicals (nitric acid + IPA) and ammonia/other sales (see _why). Net-debt company: explicit interest, no treasury yield. Valued on a sum of the parts (segment EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E, the street's method), with P/E and DCF cross-checks.

segments.name: Chemicals (TAN, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia)
segments._why: Built from three lines (FY26 -> FY27E / FY28E / FY29E, Rs cr). TAN: FY26 577 kt at Rs45/kg = Rs2,604 cr; Q1FY27 130 kt at Rs70/kg (Rs904 cr) on war-time FGAN prices, volume cut by PESO portal changes. Existing plants run ~98% full (587 ktpa); the 376 ktpa Gopalpur plant (Rs2,675 cr, 96% complete in Jul-2026, commissioning guided for Q2FY27) adds ~90 kt in FY27 (management: ~80% utilisation by Q4FY27), ~300 kt in FY28 and ~350 kt in FY29. Volume 650 / 880 / 930 kt; realisation Rs58 / 50 / 48 per kg as FGAN prices ease from the Q1 peak (Russia lifted its export ban in May-2026) but stay above FY26 = Rs3,770 / 4,400 / 4,460 cr. Industrial chemicals: FY26 Rs1,842 cr; Q1FY27 Rs490 cr with IPA volumes down 76% on propylene (RGP) curtailment; the Dahej nitric acid plant (300 ktpa WNA + 150 ktpa CNA, Rs1,983 cr, 65% of CNA tied up for 20 years) starts in H2 = Rs2,130 / 2,550 / 2,700 cr. Ammonia sales, Platinum Blasting (Australia) and other: FY26 Rs858 cr, Q1FY27 Rs488 cr on ammonia at ~$780-800/t ME FOB (May-Jun 2026) = Rs1,500 / 1,300 / 1,300 cr. Total Rs7,400 / 8,250 / 8,460 cr = growth 39.5% / 11.5% / 2.5%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin (EBIT + segment D&A): 19.0% (FY20), 27.7% (FY21), 33.1% (FY25), 27.1% (FY26, incl. a ~Rs75 cr ammonia turnaround); EBIT margin 25-31% in FY22-24. Q1FY27 EBIT Rs805 cr on Rs1,882 cr (42.8%; ~47% EBITDA): ammonia at ~$800/t against gas now partly on the 15-year Equinor contract, TAN at Rs70/kg. FY27E 37.5% = Q1 actual plus ~34% for Q2-Q4 (Rs633 cr a quarter): monsoon-soft TAN in Q2, ammonia already back to ~$600/t ME FOB by end-July (management) and $555/t Tampa in September, offset by a full quarter of Equinor gas from Q2 (management: ~Rs300 cr a year of savings at full transition) and new capacity in H2. FY28E 32% = TAN ~Rs16,000/t EBITDA on 880 kt (Emkay assumed Rs14,500/t pre-war) ~Rs1,410 cr + ammonia ~Rs550 cr + blasting services ~Rs120 cr + industrial chemicals ~Rs600 cr = ~Rs2,680 cr; FY29E 31% as Russian supply and new domestic TAN capacity (Coal India, others) cap spreads.

segments.name: Fertilisers (Mahadhan crop nutrition)
segments._why: FY25 Rs5,120 cr, FY26 Rs6,166 cr (+20%, traded fertilisers Rs1,760 cr); Q1FY27 Rs1,367 cr (+9% YoY) with ANP/Smartek volume +1% and Bensulf -44% on sulphur costs. Kharif 2026 NBS outlay Rs41,534 cr (+12% vs Kharif 2025, approved Apr-2026); the 2026 monsoon ended at ~87% of normal (IMD, 30-Sep-2026) though Central India, Deepak's core Maharashtra market, got ~97%. Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates were not announced by 30-Sep-2026 and are not in our numbers. FY27E +2% (weak Kharif volumes, higher prices), then +6% a year (specialty and Croptek, ~40% of segment revenue in Q1FY27).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 6.6% (FY20), 10.0% (FY21), 9.6% (FY25), 8.1% (FY26); EBIT margin 0.0% in FY24 when phosphoric acid costs ran ahead of subsidy. Q1FY27 EBIT Rs44 cr (3.2%; ~4.6% EBITDA) with phosphoric acid at $1,360/t CFR (Jun-2026) and subsidy lagging costs. FY27E 5.5% (Q1 plus a partial catch-up in H2 if Rabi rates follow costs, which is not assured); FY28E 7.5% and FY29E 8.0% = mid-cycle, below FY25.

segments.name: Realty & others
segments._why: Realty (Pune mall/offices) Rs22 cr and others (furniture trading) Rs14 cr in FY26; segment EBITDA ~Rs1.5 cr. Kept flat-ish at break-even.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated costs net of other income in segment results
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: Rs185 cr (FY20), Rs173 cr (FY21), Rs256 cr (FY25), Rs248 cr (FY26). It is corporate cost plus the other income (Rs103 cr in FY26) that the company books inside 'unallocable expenditure net of unallocable income' but Screener shows below EBITDA. Rs260 / 270 / 280 cr as head-office costs grow with the subsidiaries (DMSL, MAL) being readied for listing.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs1,570 cr (purchase of PPE incl. CWIP). Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid together cost ~Rs4,650 cr, of which ~Rs3,850 cr was spent by Q1FY27 (Q1FY27 capex Rs515 cr). CFO (29-May-2026): 'almost Rs800-1,000 crores capex spending, including maintenance' in FY27, then 'a normal maintenance capex'. We use Rs950 cr in FY27E, Rs500 cr in FY28E (maintenance plus upgrading the Chardham explosives unit bought for Rs121 cr in May-2026) and Rs600 cr in FY29E (no new large project is announced; management says the next phase comes after stabilisation, which is a risk to this number).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs424 cr; Q1FY27 Rs105 cr (~Rs420 cr a year) before the new plants. The engine holds CWIP (Rs3,053 cr at Mar-26, mostly Gopalpur and Dahej) flat and only adds FY27-29 capex to the gross block, so the ~Rs4,650 cr of new plant would never be depreciated at FY26's rate. We set the rate so that FY28-29E depreciation (~Rs640-660 cr) includes the new plants (~Rs4,650 cr at ~4.5% = ~Rs210 cr a year on top of ~Rs430 cr). FY27E (~Rs600 cr) is overstated by ~Rs80-100 cr because the plants start only in H2.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt company: borrowings incl. leases Rs5,670 cr vs cash, bank balances and liquid funds ~Rs660 cr at Mar-26 (company net debt Rs4,824 cr; Rs4,719 cr at Jun-26). Interest earned on cash is in 'other income' below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. FY26 other income Rs103 cr (annual report note 29) = interest on deposits Rs24 cr + interest on an income-tax refund Rs17 cr (one-off) + gain on selling mutual funds Rs20 cr (the Rs126 cr of funds were fully sold by Jun-26) + realised hedging gains Rs28 cr (volatile) + other Rs14 cr. Q1FY27 Rs6 cr; TTM (Q2FY26-Q1FY27) Rs85 cr. Recurring base = interest on ~Rs350-450 cr of cash (~Rs20 cr) + miscellaneous (~Rs10-15 cr): Rs30 cr in FY27E (Q1 run-rate Rs24 cr), Rs35 / 40 cr as cash rebuilds. Hedging gains and refund interest are left out.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY25 Rs413 cr, FY26 Rs353 cr after capitalising Rs116 cr of project interest (annual report note 34; gross interest Rs425 cr at 8.6-9.5%); Q1FY27 Rs95 cr. Capitalisation stops when Gopalpur and Dahej start (H2FY27), so P&L interest rises to ~Rs115 cr a quarter: FY27E Rs430 cr. FY28-29E fall with debt (model net debt ~Rs3,400 cr at Mar-28E and ~Rs2,300 cr at Mar-29E; project loans amortise from Dec-2027): Rs380 / 310 cr, incl. the 8% coupon on the liability part of DMSL's Rs800 cr CCDs.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 26.9% (FY26), 20.6% (FY25, incl. a one-time Rs40 cr credit), ~25% (Q1FY27); statutory 25.17%. No minority line is needed through FY29E: the Rs800 cr DMSL CCDs convert only at the end of 48 months (around May-2029, FY30) and their coupon is in interest; we deduct the holders' claim in the sum of the parts instead.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs10 a share for FY25 and FY26 (13.5% and 17% of EPS). We assume 17% / 17% / 20% of EPS: debt reduction comes first.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate. Net debt ~Rs4,700 cr against a market value of ~Rs17,000 cr: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~78%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.6% (8.8% pre-tax) weighted ~22% = WACC ~11.7%, which is what beta 0.87 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward 6 months.
dcf._tgWhy: Nitrogen chemicals and fertiliser demand grow with mining, infrastructure and farm output: 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~4% (FY29E) to 6% by year 10: volumes grow with mining and nitric acid demand; no new plant is assumed.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts from ~18.6% (FY29E) to 17.5% as war-time spreads keep normalising; FY21-26 averaged ~17.6%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~4% of revenue (maintenance and debottlenecking); depreciation 4.2% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: War-time spreads last into FY28: ammonia stays near $600/t, TAN near Rs55/kg, Gopalpur fills in a year and Rabi subsidies catch up with costs, so Chemicals margins hold at ~36% and Fertilisers recover to ~9-10%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Spreads go back to pre-war levels by FY28 (ammonia ~$400/t, TAN ~Rs45/kg as Russian supply returns and new Indian capacity arrives), Gopalpur ramps slowly and subsidies keep lagging: Chemicals margins ~29% / 28% (pre-war spreads plus the Equinor saving) and Fertilisers ~5.5-6%.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Deepak Fertilisers: the only detailed broker method we found (Emkay, Nov-2025) is a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA (DMSL 12x, industrial chemicals 10x, crop nutrition 6x). The segments differ in quality and returns, debt is material, and management plans to list DMSL and MAL separately. We value the reported segments on Sep-28E EBITDA (Chemicals 7x, Fertilisers 6x), less corporate costs, the CCD holders' claim and net debt at Sep-27E.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check. One-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 is 9.7x leaving out FY24 as a trough year (EPS Rs35.9 vs Rs95.9 in FY23; 11.5x including it); peers traded a median ~12% below their five-year P/E medians on 30-Sep-2026 -> 8.5x on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 11x (the post-Apr-2023 median), bear 7x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Cross-check: 10-year FCFF at ~11.7% (beta 0.87 so that the single discount rate equals WACC), terminal growth 5.5%, EBITDA margin fading to 17.5%, less net debt at Mar-27E.

cover.headline: India's TAN leader is about to get much bigger, but a war-time windfall is being priced as if it will last
cover.lead: Deepak Fertilisers makes ~40% of India's technical ammonium nitrate (TAN, the base of mining explosives), most of its concentrated nitric acid, its own ammonia (500 ktpa at Taloja) and Mahadhan fertilisers. Two projects worth ~₹4,650 cr (Gopalpur TAN, Dahej nitric acid) are due to start in Q2FY27 (we assume output from Q3), and a 15-year Equinor gas contract began in May-2026. Q1FY27 was a record (EBITDA ₹845 cr, 26% margin) because the Middle East war pushed ammonia to ~$800/t and TAN to ~₹70/kg. Those prices were already falling by end-September. We forecast EPS of ₹110.0 / 109.7 / 115.4 for FY27-29E: higher volumes roughly offset fading spreads. The street (Emkay) values the stock on a **sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA**; we do the same on Sep-28E: Chemicals at **7x** and Fertilisers at **6x** (from the stock's own forward-multiple history, de-rated with the sector), less corporate costs, the DMSL convertible holders' claim and net debt. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** P/E (₹957 at 8.5x) and DCF (₹1,436) bracket it. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A real TAN franchise that grows 64% in capacity
arguments.p: TAN volumes rose from 519 kt (FY25) to 577 kt (FY26) at ~98% utilisation; Gopalpur adds 376 ktpa on the east coast, next to the coal belt, taking capacity to ~963 ktpa. Deepak is the only Indian maker of low- and high-density AN, sells 17% of TAN revenue through mine-site services (B2C) and has bought an explosives unit (Chardham, ₹121 cr). Dahej adds 450 ktpa of nitric acid, 65% of the concentrated grade pre-sold for 20 years.

arguments.h: Q1FY27 was a windfall, not a run-rate
arguments.p: Chemicals EBIT was ₹805 cr in Q1FY27, 70% of the segment's full-year FY26 EBIT (₹1,147 cr). Ammonia (bulk FOB Middle East) went from ~$300/t in mid-2025 to $801/t in May-2026; it was ~$600 by end-July and Tampa ammonia fell for a fourth month in September. We put Chemicals EBITDA margins at 37.5% in FY27E and 32% in FY28E (47% in Q1), still above FY25's 33% thanks to cheaper Equinor gas.

arguments.h: Debt falls from FY28, with strings attached
arguments.p: Net debt was ₹4,719 cr at Jun-26 (company measure). Capex drops from ~₹950 cr (FY27E) to ~₹500-600 cr and we see net debt at ~₹2,590 cr by Mar-29E (Screener basis). But the ₹800 cr of DMSL convertibles carry a 12.5% yield and will take ~6-7% of the mining subsidiary; a promoter LLP bought ₹300 cr of them partly with money borrowed against pledged DFPCL shares; and the ammonia subsidiary lost ₹257 cr in FY26.

arguments.h: The price already pays for the good news
arguments.p: At ₹1,351 the stock trades at 12.3x our FY28E EPS and 7.2x FY28E EV/EBITDA. Its own one-year-forward medians since Apr-2021 are 9.7x P/E (ex-FY24 trough) and 6.8x EV/EBITDA, and fertiliser and chemical peers sit below their five-year medians. Our sum of the parts implies 6.8x Sep-28E EBITDA. Upside needs the war-time spreads to last.

sections.title: What Deepak does: turns gas into ammonia, ammonia into explosives-grade nitrate, acids and fertilisers

blocks.p: Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals (DFPCL) started in 1979 as an ammonia-based chemicals and fertiliser maker at Taloja, near Mumbai. Today it runs one value chain: natural gas (a domestic take-or-pay contract and, since May-2026, a 15-year LNG contract with Equinor of Norway) → ammonia (a 500 ktpa plant at Taloja, plus bought and traded ammonia) → nitric acid (885 ktpa weak, 231 ktpa concentrated) → technical ammonium nitrate (TAN, 587 ktpa), the oxidiser in mining and quarrying explosives. Alongside sit isopropyl alcohol (IPA, 70 ktpa, made from refinery propylene) for pharma solvents, and Mahadhan crop nutrition: complex fertilisers (NP 24:24:0, NPK), crop-specific Croptek blends, Bensulf and water-soluble fertilisers sold mainly in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat. Despite the name, fertilisers are 54% of revenue but only ~27% of segment profit; chemicals are the profit engine.

blocks.callout: **Pattern to remember:** Deepak builds big integrated assets and then lives through the commodity cycle on them. The ammonia plant arrived as ammonia prices fell (FY24) and lost money in its own books in FY26; it is earning well only now, in a war. Gopalpur arrives as TAN prices are at a peak. sections.title: Industry: TAN is short in India, ammonia is volatile, fertilisers are run by policy

blocks.p: **TAN.** India used ~1,319 kt of TAN in FY25 but made only ~916 kt and imported ~422 kt, mostly from Russia (Emkay, citing industry data). Demand follows coal and mineral output and infrastructure blasting; Q2 (monsoon) is the weak quarter and Q4 the strongest. In early 2026 Russian exports were disrupted (an export ban, lifted in May-2026, and plant incidents), which is why domestic prices jumped. New supply is coming: Deepak's own Gopalpur (376 ktpa) and, further out, Coal India's coal-gasification-based ammonium nitrate, whose technology is still unproven. **Ammonia.** Global ammonia rose from ~$300/t (mid-2025) to $801/t (May-2026) on Middle East supply losses and was falling again by September. **Fertilisers.** Phosphatic and potassic fertilisers are paid a per-kg Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) fixed each season, and the government keeps farm-gate prices in check: if phosphoric acid and sulphur rise faster than the subsidy, NPK makers' margins shrink, as in FY24 and H2FY26.

sections.title: Chemicals: a strong TAN and nitric acid franchise, with Q1FY27 profits that will not last

blocks.p: The Chemicals segment (TAN, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia and Australian blasting services) earned EBIT of ₹1,412 cr in FY25 and ₹1,147 cr in FY26 on revenue of ~₹5,100-5,300 cr, i.e. EBITDA margins of 33% and 27% once segment depreciation is added back. **TAN** is the core: 577 kt sold in FY26 (+11%) at ~98% utilisation, ₹2,604 cr of revenue, 16-17% of it from mine-site services and bulk-explosive supply (B2C), which earn more than selling bags of nitrate. **Industrial chemicals** (₹1,842 cr): 302 kt of merchant nitric acid (~45% of India's merchant market per the annual report) and 63 kt of IPA; IPA depends on refinery propylene, which the government diverted to LPG during the 2026 gas crisis, so Q1FY27 IPA volumes fell 76%. **Ammonia**: the Taloja plant made 452 kt in FY26 (~93% of group needs) and was debottlenecked ~10% in the Q4FY26 shutdown; in its own books (PCL) it lost ₹257 cr after interest and depreciation, because it sells to group plants at internal prices. In Q1FY27 everything turned: segment EBIT ₹805 cr on ₹1,882 cr (42.8%).

blocks.p: Mahadhan AgriTech sells ~₹6,200 cr a year of fertilisers: manufactured NP and NPK grades (NPK 494 kt and nitrophosphate 241 kt in FY26, both lower than FY25 as plants ran at ~54-75%), Croptek crop-specific blends (248 kt), Bensulf and water-soluble products, and ~₹1,760 cr of traded DAP/MOP. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Deepak has a **position**, not a moat. In TAN it is the largest Indian producer with the widest product range, plants on both coasts from FY27 and growing mine-site services; in concentrated nitric acid it has most of the market and long contracts. That wins volume and customers. It does not set prices: TAN, nitric acid, IPA and ammonia follow global prices and imports, and fertiliser economics are set by the subsidy. Returns show it: ROCE ran 11-25% over FY22-26 and Chemicals segment pre-tax ROCE fell from 72% (FY23) to 26.3% (FY26) as capital went into projects. We give no moat premium in the multiple.

sections.title: Quarters: three weak ones, then a ₹845 cr record in Q1FY27 on war-time prices

blocks.p: Quarterly EBITDA ran at ₹460-515 cr through FY25 and Q1FY26, slid to ₹353-354 cr in Q3-Q4FY26 (fertiliser costs ahead of subsidies, weak IPA, the ammonia turnaround), and then jumped to ₹845 cr in Q1FY27. The jump came from the Chemicals segment (EBIT ₹805 cr, 43% of its revenue): ammonia traded at ~$780-800/t FOB Middle East in May-June 2026, TAN realisations rose to ~₹70/kg (₹45/kg in FY26) as imports dried up, and the first Equinor LNG cargo (May-2026) lowered gas cost. Fertilisers earned only ₹44 cr. TAN volumes actually fell 12% (a PESO licensing-portal change) and IPA volumes 76% (propylene curtailed by the government).

sections.title: Revenue tripled in a decade; profit has followed global ammonia, not a rising line

blocks.p: Revenue rose from ₹3,808 cr in FY15 to ₹11,506 cr in FY26, but in jumps and falls: +47% in FY23 when the Russia-Ukraine war lifted ammonia, nitric acid and fertiliser prices, −23% in FY24 when they fell back, +18% and +12% in FY25-26. EBITDA tells the same story: ₹961 cr (FY21), ₹2,165 cr at the FY23 peak, ₹1,287 cr in FY24, ₹1,925 cr in FY25 and ₹1,684 cr in FY26, when phosphoric acid, sulphur and a planned ammonia shutdown (~₹75 cr) hurt. Below EBITDA the 500 ktpa ammonia plant changed the cost base: depreciation went from ₹233 cr (FY22) to ₹424 cr and interest from ₹155 cr to ₹404 cr (FY24), ₹353 cr in FY26 only because ₹116 cr was capitalised into the new projects. Then Q1FY27 broke every record: EBITDA ₹845 cr (26% margin) and profit ₹490 cr, two-thirds of FY26's full-year profit in one quarter.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a spread business. Deepak buys gas, ammonia, phosphoric acid, sulphur and propylene and sells products whose prices follow global benchmarks (TAN, nitric acid, IPA, ammonia) or government subsidy rates (fertilisers). Profit therefore moves with global spreads, as FY23-FY24 and now Q1FY27 show. What management controls is volume (Gopalpur and Dahej add ~64% to TAN and ~40% to nitric acid capacity), cost (own ammonia, the Equinor gas contract) and mix (B2C mining services, specialty fertilisers). Our forecasts lean on those, not on the war-time spreads lasting.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but capitalised interest, state incentives and a convertible shown as equity flatter the picture

bullets: **Capitalised interest.** ₹116 cr of FY26 interest (₹41 cr in FY25) was added to the cost of Gopalpur and Dahej instead of the P&L (gross interest ₹425 cr vs ₹353 cr reported). It stops at start-up, so FY27-28 interest rises even if debt falls; we model ₹430 cr for FY27E.

**State incentives inside revenue.** Gujarat and Maharashtra investment incentives of ₹109 cr (FY26) and ₹204 cr (FY25) are booked as revenue, i.e. inside EBITDA; ₹403 cr was still receivable from the states at Mar-26. Emkay estimated the GST cut (18% → 5%) lowers the Maharashtra incentive by ₹120-140 cr a year.
**Other income is not all recurring.** FY26 other income of ₹103 cr included ₹17 cr of interest on a tax refund, ₹20 cr of mutual-fund gains and ₹28 cr of hedging gains; we forecast only ₹30-40 cr.

**A convertible shown as equity.** DMSL's ₹800 cr CCDs pay 8% in cash, target a 12.5% annual return and carry an investor put on specified events, yet ₹619 cr of them sits in equity (as minority interest) and only ₹181 cr in debt. Economically, net debt is understated by up to ~₹619 cr; we deduct that amount in our valuation.

**Transfer prices hide where the profit is.** The ammonia subsidiary sells to group plants at internal prices and lost ₹257 cr in FY26; TAN and nitric acid show the benefit. The company does not report ammonia, TAN and industrial-chemical profit separately.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was ₹206 cr in FY26 on EBITDA of ₹1,684 cr (₹1,880 cr in FY25), as receivables rose ₹728 cr (incl. subsidy ₹751 cr owed by the government) and inventory ₹669 cr. Management called it a temporary Kharif build-up.
**One-offs.** Q4FY26: ~₹70-75 cr ammonia turnaround and ₹20 cr labour-code charge. FY25: a one-time tax credit of ₹40 cr.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** P G Bhagwat LLP gave an unmodified opinion with no emphasis of matter; key audit matters were the CCD accounting and contingent liabilities. Seven subsidiaries holding ₹10,613 cr of assets were audited by other firms, database-level audit trails ran only from Oct-2025, and CARO remarks cover cash losses at PCL. We see no sign of manipulation, but reported EBITDA includes state incentives, interest was capitalised during construction, and the CCD treatment makes leverage look lower than it is.

sections.title: Net debt peaked near ₹4,800 cr; the projects are paid for, the cash has to follow

blocks.p: Two building cycles explain the debt. The ammonia plant took net debt from ~₹1,500 cr (FY22) to ~₹3,500 cr (FY24); Gopalpur and Dahej (FY25-27) took it to ₹4,824 cr at Mar-26 on the company's measure (₹5,001 cr on Screener's, which also counts ₹184 cr of leases and the ₹181 cr debt part of DMSL's CCDs). FY26 was a poor cash year: operating cash flow was only ₹206 cr on ₹1,684 cr of EBITDA because receivables rose by ₹728 cr (subsidy due from the government ₹751 cr, up from ₹619 cr) and inventory by ₹669 cr. Q1FY27's profits brought net debt down to ₹4,719 cr (1.4x annualised EBITDA) even after ₹515 cr of capex. Over FY19-26 Deepak generated ₹7,658 cr of operating cash and spent ₹7,199 cr on plants.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise at a peak, with a price that assumes the peak lasts

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest maker of technical ammonium nitrate (~40% share, going to ~963 ktpa), its main concentrated nitric acid supplier, a 500 ktpa ammonia plant fed by a 15-year LNG contract, and a regional fertiliser brand (Mahadhan) whose margins depend on subsidy policy. Q1FY27 EBIT Rs805 cr on Rs1,882 cr (42.8%; ~47% EBITDA): ammonia at ~$800/t against gas now partly on the 15-year Equinor contract, TAN at Rs70/kg. FY27E 37.5% = Q1 actual plus ~34% for Q2-Q4 (Rs633 cr a quarter): monsoon-soft TAN in Q2, ammonia already back to ~$600/t ME FOB by end-July (management) and $555/t Tampa in September, offset by a full quarter of Equinor gas from Q2 (management: ~Rs300 cr a year of savings at full transition) and new capacity in H2. segments.name: Fertilisers (Mahadhan crop nutrition)
segments._why: FY25 Rs5,120 cr, FY26 Rs6,166 cr (+20%, traded fertilisers Rs1,760 cr); Q1FY27 Rs1,367 cr (+9% YoY) with ANP/Smartek volume +1% and Bensulf -44% on sulphur costs. Kharif 2026 NBS outlay Rs41,534 cr (+12% vs Kharif 2025, approved Apr-2026); the 2026 monsoon ended at ~87% of normal (IMD, 30-Sep-2026) though Central India, Deepak's core Maharashtra market, got ~97%. Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates were not announced by 30-Sep-2026 and are not in our numbers. FY27E +2% (weak Kharif volumes, higher prices), then +6% a year (specialty and Croptek, ~40% of segment revenue in Q1FY27).
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 6.6% (FY20), 10.0% (FY21), 9.6% (FY25), 8.1% (FY26); EBIT margin 0.0% in FY24 when phosphoric acid costs ran ahead of subsidy. Q1FY27 EBIT Rs44 cr (3.2%; ~4.6% EBITDA) with phosphoric acid at $1,360/t CFR (Jun-2026) and subsidy lagging costs. FY27E 5.5% (Q1 plus a partial catch-up in H2 if Rabi rates follow costs, which is not assured); FY28E 7.5% and FY29E 8.0% = mid-cycle, below FY25.

segments.name: Realty & others
segments._why: Realty (Pune mall/offices) Rs22 cr and others (furniture trading) Rs14 cr in FY26; segment EBITDA ~Rs1.5 cr. Kept flat-ish at break-even.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated costs net of other income in segment results
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: Rs185 cr (FY20), Rs173 cr (FY21), Rs256 cr (FY25), Rs248 cr (FY26). It is corporate cost plus the other income (Rs103 cr in FY26) that the company books inside 'unallocable expenditure net of unallocable income' but Screener shows below EBITDA. Rs260 / 270 / 280 cr as head-office costs grow with the subsidiaries (DMSL, MAL) being readied for listing.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs1,570 cr (purchase of PPE incl. CWIP). Gopalpur TAN and Dahej nitric acid together cost ~Rs4,650 cr, of which ~Rs3,850 cr was spent by Q1FY27 (Q1FY27 capex Rs515 cr). CFO (29-May-2026): 'almost Rs800-1,000 crores capex spending, including maintenance' in FY27, then 'a normal maintenance capex'. We use Rs950 cr in FY27E, Rs500 cr in FY28E (maintenance plus upgrading the Chardham explosives unit bought for Rs121 cr in May-2026) and Rs600 cr in FY29E (no new large project is announced; management says the next phase comes after stabilisation, which is a risk to this number).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs424 cr; Q1FY27 Rs105 cr (~Rs420 cr a year) before the new plants. The engine holds CWIP (Rs3,053 cr at Mar-26, mostly Gopalpur and Dahej) flat and only adds FY27-29 capex to the gross block, so the ~Rs4,650 cr of new plant would never be depreciated at FY26's rate. We set the rate so that FY28-29E depreciation (~Rs640-660 cr) includes the new plants (~Rs4,650 cr at ~4.5% = ~Rs210 cr a year on top of ~Rs430 cr). FY27E (~Rs600 cr) is overstated by ~Rs80-100 cr because the plants start only in H2.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net-debt company: borrowings incl. leases Rs5,670 cr vs cash, bank balances and liquid funds ~Rs660 cr at Mar-26 (company net debt Rs4,824 cr; Rs4,719 cr at Jun-26). Interest earned on cash is in 'other income' below.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built, not plugged. FY26 other income Rs103 cr (annual report note 29) = interest on deposits Rs24 cr + interest on an income-tax refund Rs17 cr (one-off) + gain on selling mutual funds Rs20 cr (the Rs126 cr of funds were fully sold by Jun-26) + realised hedging gains Rs28 cr (volatile) + other Rs14 cr. Q1FY27 Rs6 cr; TTM (Q2FY26-Q1FY27) Rs85 cr. Recurring base = interest on ~Rs350-450 cr of cash (~Rs20 cr) + miscellaneous (~Rs10-15 cr): Rs30 cr in FY27E (Q1 run-rate Rs24 cr), Rs35 / 40 cr as cash rebuilds. Hedging gains and refund interest are left out.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY25 Rs413 cr, FY26 Rs353 cr after capitalising Rs116 cr of project interest (annual report note 34; gross interest Rs425 cr at 8.6-9.5%); Q1FY27 Rs95 cr. Capitalisation stops when Gopalpur and Dahej start (H2FY27), so P&L interest rises to ~Rs115 cr a quarter: FY27E Rs430 cr. FY28-29E fall with debt (model net debt ~Rs3,400 cr at Mar-28E and ~Rs2,300 cr at Mar-29E; project loans amortise from Dec-2027): Rs380 / 310 cr, incl. the 8% coupon on the liability part of DMSL's Rs800 cr CCDs.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 26.9% (FY26), 20.6% (FY25, incl. a one-time Rs40 cr credit), ~25% (Q1FY27); statutory 25.17%. No minority line is needed through FY29E: the Rs800 cr DMSL CCDs convert only at the end of 48 months (around May-2029, FY30) and their coupon is in interest; we deduct the holders' claim in the sum of the parts instead.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs10 a share for FY25 and FY26 (13.5% and 17% of EPS). We assume 17% / 17% / 20% of EPS: debt reduction comes first.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts free cash flow at one rate. Net debt ~Rs4,700 cr against a market value of ~Rs17,000 cr: cost of equity ~13.1% (beta 1.1) weighted ~78%, post-tax cost of debt ~6.6% (8.8% pre-tax) weighted ~22% = WACC ~11.7%, which is what beta 0.87 produces. The same rate rolls the value forward 6 months.
dcf._tgWhy: Nitrogen chemicals and fertiliser demand grow with mining, infrastructure and farm output: 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~4% (FY29E) to 6% by year 10: volumes grow with mining and nitric acid demand; no new plant is assumed.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin drifts from ~18.6% (FY29E) to 17.5% as war-time spreads keep normalising; FY21-26 averaged ~17.6%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~4% of revenue (maintenance and debottlenecking); depreciation 4.2% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: War-time spreads last into FY28: ammonia stays near $600/t, TAN near Rs55/kg, Gopalpur fills in a year and Rabi subsidies catch up with costs, so Chemicals margins hold at ~36% and Fertilisers recover to ~9-10%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Spreads go back to pre-war levels by FY28 (ammonia ~$400/t, TAN ~Rs45/kg as Russian supply returns and new Indian capacity arrives), Gopalpur ramps slowly and subsidies keep lagging: Chemicals margins ~29% / 28% (pre-war spreads plus the Equinor saving) and Fertilisers ~5.5-6%.

parts.name: Chemicals
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E + half FY29E) x EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Derived, not picked: the stock's one-year-forward EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 is 6.8x (no EBITDA trough year; 6.8x since Apr-2023, 8.0x since Apr-2024); peers traded a median ~5% below their five-year EV/EBITDA medians on 30-Sep-2026 -> 6.5x for the group. At the FY25-26 mix (Chemicals 76% of segment EBITDA) and Fertilisers at 6x, that implies ~6.6-6.7x for Chemicals; rounded up to 7x because Gopalpur and Dahej fill over two years. Street: Emkay 12x DMSL, 10x industrial chemicals (Nov-2025). Bull 9x, bear 6x.

parts.name: Fertilisers
parts.note: Fertiliser peers excluding Coromandel (Chambal, Paradeep, GNFC, GSFC, RCF) trade at a median ~5.8x trailing EV/EBITDA (five-year median ~7.4x); Emkay uses 6x for crop nutrition. Policy-set margins, sub-scale NPK: 6x (bull 7x, bear 5x).

parts.note: The equity component of DMSL's Rs800 cr CCDs (Rs619 cr, shown as non-controlling interest at Mar-26). The CCDs convert into DMSL shares at 48 months (stake not disclosed; Emkay ~6-7%); their Rs181 cr debt component is already in net debt.

parts.name: Less: net debt at Sep-27E

parts.note: Model forecast: borrowings incl. leases less cash and investments.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Deepak Fertilisers: the only detailed broker method we found (Emkay, Nov-2025) is a sum of the parts on EV/EBITDA (DMSL 12x, industrial chemicals 10x, crop nutrition 6x). The segments differ in quality and returns, debt is material, and management plans to list DMSL and MAL separately. We value the reported segments on Sep-28E EBITDA (Chemicals 7x, Fertilisers 6x), less corporate costs, the CCD holders' claim and net debt at Sep-27E.

methods.name: P/E

methods.why: Cross-check: 10-year FCFF at ~11.7% (beta 0.87 so that the single discount rate equals WACC), terminal growth 5.5%, EBITDA margin fading to 17.5%, less net debt at Mar-27E.
